newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold easier in Europe, seen in $340/342 range.
newsitem.headline: Gold easier in Europe, seen in $340/342 range.

text.p: Gold opened marginally easier in calm European trading on Monday, and dealers said they expected a narrow range to prevail in technical dealing.
The market was unlikely to react very much to the European Union summit meeting in Amsterdam.
"This is not very important for gold at the moment," one dealer at a major Swiss bank said, adding he thought gold would move within a range of $340 to $342 an ounce on Monday.
Gold opened at $340.75/$341.05, down from $341.30/$341.80 at the London close on Friday.
Silver opened at $4.69/$4.71, down three cents from Friday's close, and was expected to track gold.
Platinum shed $7 to $430.00/$435.00, while palladium was unchanged at $202.00/$207.00.
Trading was expected to be less volatile than of late but prices remained underpinned by Russian supply concerns, traders said.
